## Purpose
Implements the per-run Server-Sent Events down-channel, `GET /api/runs/{id}/events/stream` — the browser-native, resumable (via `Last-Event-ID`) replacement for the retired `/ws/chat` WebSocket transport. It replays the durable event log past the client's cursor, sends a `stream_attached` handshake, re-arms a still-open human review gate on reload, then drains live events until the run terminates or the client disconnects.

## Shape
- `_sse_body` / `_sse_frame` — render one event as an SSE frame dict (`id:` = durable `seq`, `data:` = single-line `{type, data}` JSON), matching a shared wire-parity contract also used by a characterization test.
- `_dangling_review_gate` — finds the last still-open `review_gate_ready` row (one bounded query) so a reload during a paused gate can re-open it.
- `_iter_sse_frames` — the core generator: durable replay → handshake → D-14g gate re-arm → live queue drain, all wrapped in one try/finally that always unsubscribes from the per-run fan-out bus.
- `stream_run_events` — the route handler: two-layer owner check (ORM filter + `ScopedStore.get_run`, both IDOR→404), resolves the resume cursor, subscribes to the live queue only if the run is actually live, and wraps the generator with open/close logging.

## Why this shape
The module docstring frames this as one half of a deliberate transport cutover (CHAT-07/D-01/D-13) whose frames must stay wire-identical to the old WebSocket frames (verified against a shared `_sse_projection` test module) so no client-side consumer needed to change; the pre-stream owner checks use a request-scoped DB session while the streaming generator uses a separate session-less `ScopedStore`, because FastAPI tears down the `get_db` session before the streaming body runs and reusing it would leak a pooled connection per open stream (documented as BUG-004).
